skill.name: file-uploads
skill.description: Guides secure file upload design for S3, Cloudflare R2, presigned URLs, multipart transfers, validation, and safe handling of large files.
skill.summary: Design secure, scalable file upload and cloud storage workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Unsafe uploads can expose systems, exhaust resources, and leak private files. This skill provides practical patterns for validation, storage, and scalable transfer workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains MIME validation with magic-byte detection instead of trusting extensions or client headers.
Shows server and client upload size limits that reduce memory, disk, and storage abuse.
Prevents path traversal by removing path components, restricting extensions, and generating unique filenames.
Recommends short-lived presigned URLs and no-store response headers for private files.
Guides direct and streamed upload designs that avoid buffering large files on application servers.
limitations: Provides implementation guidance but does not execute uploads, configure cloud accounts, or deploy infrastructure.
Uses JavaScript and TypeScript examples that require adaptation for other languages and frameworks.
Does not provide a complete IAM policy, malware scanner, or storage lifecycle configuration.
Mentions image optimization but does not include a complete optimization pipeline.

use_cases.title: Secure an Upload Endpoint
use_cases.description: Review validation, size limits, filename handling, and response behavior for a web application upload endpoint.

use_cases.title: Design Direct Cloud Uploads
use_cases.description: Plan presigned uploads to S3 or R2 while controlling object names, file sizes, expiry, and caching.

use_cases.title: Audit Upload Threats
use_cases.description: Identify file spoofing, path traversal, denial-of-service, and private URL exposure in an existing upload flow.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Upload Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this upload requirement: {requirement}. Recommend allowed file types, a size limit, and safe filename handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a concise security checklist before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Upload Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this upload endpoint: {implementation}. Identify weak validation, buffering, path traversal, and unsafe content serving. Suggest specific fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer has an existing server-side upload implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Presigned Upload Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a presigned upload flow for {provider} and {file_types}. Include authorization, object keys, size enforcement, expiry, caching, and post-upload validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs direct uploads to S3 or Cloudflare R2.

prompt_templates.title: Threat Model a Large Upload System
prompt_templates.prompt: Threat model this multipart upload architecture: {architecture}. Cover abuse cases, resource limits, private access, validation stages, failure recovery, and monitoring controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced team is reviewing a high-volume upload platform.

output_examples.input: Review an image upload endpoint that checks only the filename extension.
output: Critical issue: extensions and client content types can be forged.
Detect the actual format from file signatures and allow only approved MIME types.
Generate a new storage name and serve the object with the validated content type.

output_examples.input: Design uploads for videos up to five gigabytes without routing bytes through the application server.
output: Use authorized, short-lived multipart upload URLs for direct cloud transfer.
Bind object keys and expected sizes to the authenticated user and upload record.
Validate the completed object before publication and remove abandoned multipart uploads.

output_examples.input: Assess how a private download URL should be returned from an API.
output_examples.output: Return a short-lived signed URL only after authorization. Mark the API response as non-cacheable and avoid logging or sharing the URL.

best_practices: Validate actual file signatures, size, and authorization before making an uploaded object available.
Generate storage keys on the server and keep original filenames as untrusted display metadata.
Use short expiry periods, private storage defaults, and non-cacheable responses for sensitive signed URLs.
anti_patterns: Do not trust filename extensions or client-provided content types as proof of file format.
Do not buffer large uploads in application memory or accept uploads without enforced size limits.
Do not concatenate user filenames into filesystem paths or public object keys.

faq.question: Does this skill upload files for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides design and review guidance for implementing file upload and storage workflows.

faq.question: Which storage services does it cover?
faq.answer: It addresses patterns for Amazon S3 and Cloudflare R2, especially direct uploads and signed URLs.

faq.question: Why are filename extensions insufficient?
faq.answer: Attackers can rename files or forge content headers. Verify the format from file signatures and enforce an allowlist.

faq.question: How should large files be handled?
faq.answer: Stream data or use direct multipart cloud uploads. Enforce size limits without buffering the full file in application memory.

faq.question: How does it prevent path traversal?
faq.answer: It recommends removing path components, allowing limited extensions, and generating new server-controlled filenames.

faq.question: Does it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. Validate the final implementation, permissions, provider settings, and threat controls in the target environment.
